name: two letters change per slide
hook: Looking for an anagram of one string inside another? Don't re-sort every window. Each slide changes two letters: {brute_reads} characters read becomes {fast_reads}.
hook_slide: Don't re-check the window. *Two letters changed.*
hook_sub: Finding an anagram of one string inside another.
caption: Does s2 contain a permutation of s1 as a contiguous substring? Two strings are anagrams exactly when their letter counts match, so slide a window the length of s1 across s2 and compare counts.
Re-reading and sorting every window: with s1 of {k} letters and s2 of {n}, that is {windows} windows and {brute_reads} characters read.

But the window never changes size. Each slide, one character leaves and one enters, so at most 2 letters' counts change. Keep a single number, how many of the 26 letters currently have equal counts, and update it for just those letters. {fast_reads} characters read, same answer.
It is the fixed-window sum trick with a frequency map underneath instead of a number.
What else can you slide instead of recompute? 👇

p: Two strings are anagrams exactly when their letter counts match.
It is always `len(s1)` long. Each slide, one character leaves and one enters.

slides.h: One letter changed? Re-check one letter.
p: A match can only be broken, or made, at the letter that just changed.
When `matches` is 26, every letter agrees: the window is an anagram.
The fixed-window sum trick, with a frequency map underneath instead of a number.
